nodes.name: seed-vantai.sql
nodes.summary: Clean-slate demo seed for vantai.tingting.vip: truncates ~35 tables with CASCADE, resets sequences, then loads realistic Vietnamese trucking data — 9 users (password 123456), 7 trucks, 6 trailers, 6 drivers, 7 suppliers, 10 real logistics customers, 12 Hai Phong routes with JSONB default legs, pricing and road-allowance tables, fuel config, container types, and 14 ports — plus 30 trips across May–June 2026 with legs, forwarder expenses, ledger entries, and vehicle expenses.
nodes.languageNotes: Idempotent-by-wipe pattern: TRUNCATE ... CASCADE plus ALTER SEQUENCE ... RESTART yields deterministic IDs, so later INSERTs can reference master rows positionally.

nodes.name: seed-vantai-6months.sql
nodes.summary: Extended variant of the vantai demo seed that spreads the same master data across six months of trips (VT-2601 through VT-2606, almost entirely LOCKED, with trip code counters per month) and randomized created_at/updated_at timestamps — built to exercise monthly reporting, salary-period, and AR-aging screens.
nodes.languageNotes: Jitters event timestamps with 'date'::timestamp + interval '8 hours' + (random() * interval '8 hours') so each trip lands at a plausible hour of its departure day.

nodes.name: seed-staging-quytrinh.sql
nodes.summary: Additive, idempotent staging upsert of real customer master data from the 2026-07-30 Excel delivery: Silver Sea company identity into app_settings, the Long Minh partner/supplier/customer triple (MST 2300540419, 15-day freight payment terms), the 19-column 'MAU DEBIT LONG MINH' debit-note template stored as a JSONB column layout, and a repoint of the khachhang portal user to the Long Minh customer. Preserves existing demo trips and users.
nodes.languageNotes: Works around expression-based unique indexes (lower(btrim(...))) with NOT EXISTS guards plus follow-up UPDATEs, because expression indexes cannot be ON CONFLICT inference targets.

nodes.name: seed-staging-quytrinh-sites.sql
nodes.summary: Deferred staging seed that upserts 8 Long Minh operational sites from the customer's DATA PM Excel — 3 NEWEB warehouses (Ha Nam/Ninh Binh), 2 ASKEY factories, SUNRISE, SJ Tech, and S-CONNECT (Bac Ninh) — each with Google Maps links, lift-fee invoice details, and driver-facing strict_rules. It requires migration 0170 (operational_sites), so it must be applied only after a backend image redeploy.
nodes.languageNotes: Idempotency via ON CONFLICT (customer_id, code) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL — a partial-index conflict target — refreshing every column on re-run.

nodes.name: seed-staging-2026-08-05-customer-sites.sql
nodes.summary: Staging hotfix for the empty factory dropdown (DEF-20260804-002): upserts operational sites for Bien Bac (factory + warehouse), XNK Ha Noi (ICD warehouse + Bac Son factory), and a Long Minh smoke-test factory, mirroring the backend TypeScript seeder committed in 6d2c0bd.

nodes.name: setup-silversea-server.sh
nodes.summary: One-time, idempotent provisioning script for the prod server silversea.tingting.vip, run via `make deploy-server-setup`: 11 steps covering DNS sanity, Docker install, /opt/silversea layout, fresh secret generation with shared keys mirrored from the demo .env, compose push, nginx + certbot with a webroot HTTP-01 certificate, auto-renew hooks with a dry-run proof, ufw/SSH hardening, and finally starting postgres + redis for `make deploy` to fill in.
nodes.languageNotes: Fails closed on DNS mismatch before touching the server, and creates .env only when absent so re-runs never rotate production secrets.

nodes.name: silversea-server-db-backup.sh
nodes.summary: Pre-deploy safety net that pg_dumps the production database via docker exec, discovering POSTGRES_USER/POSTGRES_DB from the container environment; it aborts the deploy when the dump is suspiciously small on a populated database, keeping the suspect file for inspection.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs its whole remote logic through an `ssh bash -s` heredoc so the script lives in the repo while executing entirely server-side.

nodes.name: drizzle.config.ts
nodes.summary: Drizzle Kit configuration for the backend: points schema generation at the src/db/schema/index.ts barrel, emits migrations to ./drizzle with the PostgreSQL dialect, and sources the connection URL from DATABASE_URL (defaulting to the local dev Postgres on port 5441).

nodes.name: model.conf
nodes.summary: Casbin authorization model defining a subject/object/action request schema with an allow-if-any policy effect and matchers that honor wildcards ("*" matches any object or action) for backend RBAC enforcement.
nodes.languageNotes: Classic Casbin ACL model: the matcher supports per-subject wildcard grants, which is how the ADMIN role gets universal access via a single policy row.

nodes.name: policy.csv
nodes.summary: Casbin RBAC policy matrix granting per-role permissions across ~25 resources (trips, shipments, treasury, salary, portals, geotag) for ADMIN, MANAGER, DISPATCHER, ACCOUNTANT, CUS, OPS, DRIVER, and CUSTOMER roles, with inline comments documenting wave-by-wave access decisions such as separating dispatch resources from broad shipment access.

nodes.name: treasury.ts
nodes.summary: Drizzle schema for the treasury/financial-close domain defining six tables: debt offsets, treasury accounts, payment receipts, append-only treasury movements, payment allocations, and payment refunds. Partial unique indexes enforce idempotent posting, single-movement-per-receipt, and single-reversal rules at the database level.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Drizzle partial unique indexes (uniqueIndex(...).where(sql`...`)) to encode business invariants — e.g. a POSTED movement is unique per (account, direction, physicalReference) — a pattern stronger than plain uniqueness for append-only ledgers.

nodes.name: debtOffsets
nodes.summary: debt_offsets table storing customer/supplier debt offset records with amount, offset date, currency, minutes-document hash, and a PENDING-default approval workflow; partner linkage is intentionally nullable for legacy-row upgrade safety.

nodes.name: treasuryAccounts
nodes.summary: treasury_accounts table defining cash/bank accounts with opening balances, cutover timestamps, governance-linked opening actions, optimistic versioning, and DRAFT-default lifecycle status.

nodes.name: paymentReceipts
nodes.summary: payment_receipts table recording customer payments with received/allocated/unapplied/refunded amount breakdowns, allocation method, idempotency request hash, and payment-contract versioning.

nodes.name: treasuryMovements
nodes.summary: Append-only treasury_movements book ledger linked to one physical collection/payment source, with direction, value date, reversal-of linkage, and four partial unique indexes guaranteeing one POSTED movement per physical reference, receipt, ledger entry, and reversal.

nodes.name: paymentAllocations
nodes.summary: payment_allocations table splitting a single receipt across multiple trips or billing documents, snapshotting due dates at allocation time and supporting OLDEST_FIRST, PROPORTIONAL, and MANUAL strategies with per-receipt order/target uniqueness.

nodes.name: paymentRefunds
nodes.summary: payment_refunds table recording approved refunds tied one-to-one to a governance action and ledger entry, with mandatory reason and maker/approver attribution.

nodes.name: locked-entity-manifest.ts
nodes.summary: Governance manifest binding locked-entity rules to named TypeScript declarations and executable test proofs: each entity's terminal states, direct-mutation boundary, reopen policy, and governed actions are pinned to specific source symbols and Vitest test names so the inventory can be machine-verified against the AST rather than trusted as prose.
nodes.languageNotes: Bindings reference declarations by file + symbol + required code fragments instead of importing them, letting the exhaustive Q18 test resolve each binding through the TypeScript AST and fail when a refactor moves or weakens a governance boundary.

nodes.name: role-aliases.ts
nodes.summary: Backward-compatibility layer for the CLERK→CUS and FORWARDER→OPS role rename, canonicalizing legacy role names so auth and RBAC checks keep working with both spellings during the migration period.

nodes.name: canonicalizeRole
nodes.summary: Converts any role string to its canonical modern form (CLERK→CUS, FORWARDER→OPS), passing unknown roles through unchanged.

nodes.name: isLegacyRole
nodes.summary: Returns true when the given role is one of the legacy names (CLERK, FORWARDER) that still needs migration.

nodes.name: getModernRole
nodes.summary: Returns the modern replacement for a legacy role name, or null when the role is already modern or unknown.

nodes.name: areRolesEqual
nodes.summary: Compares two role strings after canonicalization so legacy and modern spellings of the same role compare equal.

nodes.name: getRoleAliasMappings
nodes.summary: Exposes the raw legacy→modern alias mapping for migration tooling and reporting.

nodes.name: customers.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated customer master data from the 2026-07-30 Excel delivery: the LONG MINH customer record with tax codes and payment terms, plus the SilverSea company identity block (address, bank account, representative) used for invoicing.
nodes.languageNotes: Marked do-not-edit-by-hand: the file is regenerated by the customer-data extractor from docs/BIẾU MẪU BÁO CÁO/*.xlsx.

nodes.name: drivers.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated roster of the customer's real drivers with names, tax codes, hometowns, and phone numbers, extracted from the delivered Excel report forms for seeding the identity tables.

nodes.name: factories.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated factory/receiver master data (NEWEB warehouses and similar) keyed by customer internal code, carrying raw receiver addresses, invoice tax details, driver docking notes, and Google Maps links.

nodes.name: fleet.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated fleet roster pairing heavy truck plates with trailer plates, assigned driver names, payload limits, and preferred-route tags, mirroring the customer's real truck-trailer combinations.

nodes.name: pricing.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated rate-card seed pairing routes with container sizes, revenue-share percentages, base prices, and surcharge-inclusive prices (VND) for the pricing tables.

nodes.name: reference.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated reference data for shipment intake: Hai Phong-area ports with e-port portal URLs, transport routes, and container type catalog.

nodes.name: samples.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated sample trip ledger rows (customer, factory, route, container number, receivable and payable breakdowns including freight, ferry fees, meals, and surcharges) used to seed realistic demo trip data.

nodes.name: vehicles.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated vehicle-class seed from the DATA PM workbook's vehicle-type sheet: license and trailer plates, inspection/license deadlines, per-axle load limits, driver assignments, and preferred routes.

nodes.name: nginx-frontend.conf
nodes.summary: Nginx server config baked into the frontend Docker image: serves the built SPA with gzip compression, security headers, one-year immutable caching for Vite-hashed static assets, and an index.html fallback for client-side routing.

nodes.name: nginx-host-silversea.conf
nodes.summary: Host-level nginx vhost for the production domain silversea.tingting.vip: terminates Let's Encrypt TLS, serves /uploads from the data volume, proxies /api/ to the backend on 127.0.0.1:3090 and everything else to the frontend on :3000, supports ACME webroot renewals, and deliberately exposes no public Adminer (SSH tunnel only).

nodes.name: nginx-host-vantai.conf
nodes.summary: Host-level nginx vhost for the demo/staging domain vantai.tingting.vip: same TLS/uploads/api/frontend proxy layout as production plus a public /adminer/ reverse proxy to the Adminer DB GUI, with Certbot-managed SSL blocks marked do-not-hand-edit.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: SSH-driven deploy pipeline for the vantai demo server: targets pull and recreate backend/frontend containers via deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml, run Drizzle migrations inside the backend container, toggle the Adminer profile, and prune stale Docker images.

nodes.name: eslint.config.mjs
nodes.summary: Root ESLint config applying typescript-eslint recommended rules to backend and shared sources while explicitly excluding the frontend (it has its own React/TanStack config), generated output, docs, deploy scripts, and all .js/.config files; downgrades no-explicit-any and unused-vars to warnings and allows Express Request type augmentation via declare global.

nodes.name: fifoAging.ts
nodes.summary: Shared FIFO aging calculator for receivables: sorts debit/credit ledger entries chronologically, applies credits against the oldest debits first, and buckets the remaining open balances into current/30/60/over-90-day aging buckets.

nodes.name: computeFifoAging
nodes.summary: Applies FIFO credit matching to a chronological debit/credit entry list and returns both the open-invoice remainder per entry and aged totals split into current, 1-30, 31-60, and over-90 day buckets relative to a reference date.

nodes.name: iso6346.ts
nodes.summary: ISO 6346 container-number toolkit: normalizes and validates the owner-code/serial format, computes the standard check digit from the letter-value mapping, and ranks typo-correction suggestions for near-miss container numbers.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the ISO 6346 check-digit algorithm (letters mapped 10-38 skipping multiples of 11, weights 2^0..2^9) plus a scored suggestion engine that mutates single digits and owner letters to propose valid alternatives.

nodes.name: normalizeContainerNumber
nodes.summary: Strips dashes and whitespace from a container number and uppercases it for canonical comparison.

nodes.name: validateContainerFormat
nodes.summary: Checks that a container number matches the ISO 6346 owner-code (3 letters + category letter) and 6-digit serial format.

nodes.name: calculateCheckDigit
nodes.summary: Computes the ISO 6346 check digit by summing letter-mapped values weighted by powers of two and mapping the sum modulo 11 onto the standard digit sequence.

nodes.name: validateCheckDigit
nodes.summary: Verifies that a full 11-character container number's trailing check digit matches the recomputed ISO 6346 value.

nodes.name: validateContainerNumber
nodes.summary: Full container-number validation combining format and check-digit checks, returning a structured result instead of a bare boolean.

nodes.name: suggestCorrections
nodes.summary: Ranks up to maxResults typo corrections for an invalid container number by mutating single digits (and owner letters) and scoring candidates whose recomputed check digit validates, preferring mutations closest to the original.

nodes.name: tripDriverSalary.ts
nodes.summary: Driver salary allocation helpers that prorate a monthly base salary over trips using a fixed 26-workday divisor (deliberately independent of per-month attendance standardWorkDays), with a fallback to the legacy route-default salary when no base is configured.

nodes.name: computeTripDriverSalary
nodes.summary: Allocates a driver's monthly base salary to a trip as baseSalary / 26 * tripWageDays, rounded to whole VND, returning 0 for non-finite or non-positive inputs.

nodes.name: resolveTripDriverSalary
nodes.summary: Resolves a trip's driver salary by preferring the configured-base allocation and falling back to the legacy route/default salary only when the driver has no usable base salary.

nodes.name: tripFormDefaults.ts
nodes.summary: Canonical fallback constants for trip-form math — fuel price per liter, loaded and empty fuel norms (L/100km), and road allowance per km — extracted from the frontend form so dispatcher calculations, form previews, and accountant P&L all use identical numbers when no fuel/road config is loaded.

nodes.name: api-paths.ts
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for frontend↔backend REST routing: 15 frozen path-map objects covering auth, trips, shipments (CUS workspace), catalogs, config entities, tires, financial, reports, driver/forwarder/OPS portals, notifications, system, and salary endpoints, with helper functions for parameterized paths.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `as const` object literals with function-valued members for parameterized routes (e.g. DETAIL: (id) => `/trips/${id}`), giving typed path builders instead of string concatenation at call sites.

nodes.name: source-authority.ts
nodes.summary: Executable source-authority vocabulary for the Q22 business chain: typed catalogs of source/dependent authority kinds, field families, and lock milestones, plus lookup functions deciding which propagation actions (RECOMPUTE, VERSION, ADJUST, REVERSE) are allowed before or after each milestone. Deliberately computes no money and mutates nothing.

nodes.name: findSourceAuthorityPolicy
nodes.summary: Looks up the authority policy row for a (source, dependent) pair from the SOURCE_AUTHORITY_POLICIES list, returning undefined for unknown pairs.

nodes.name: getSourceAuthorityActions
nodes.summary: Returns the allowed propagation actions for a (source, dependent) pair at a given phase (PRE_MILESTONE or POST_MILESTONE), defaulting to an empty list when no policy exists.

nodes.name: isSourceAuthorityActionAllowed
nodes.summary: Boolean gate answering whether a specific action on a (source, dependent) pair is permitted at the given phase — the single check call sites use before propagating a source change.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the shared contract package, re-exporting ~640 domain types, Zod schemas, label maps, and calculation helpers from the constants, types, schemas, calculations, governance, navigation, and shipment-planning modules. Backend routes, services, and the React frontend all consume domain contracts through this single entry point.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure re-export barrel: `export *` / named `export` + `export type` statements only, with zero runtime logic, so 642 symbols surface through one module entry.

nodes.name: pageCatalog.ts
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for SPA page metadata — the canonical path and Vietnamese title for every route (dashboard, dispatch, fleet, finance, config catalogs, driver and forwarder portals, ops field pages) exposed as the typed PAGE_CATALOG constant. Static pages carry literal paths while dynamic pages provide param-based URL builders plus route patterns, deliberately leaving RBAC to App.tsx and Casbin.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `as const satisfies Record<string, PageCatalogEntry>` so every entry keeps its literal type while still conforming to the static/dynamic entry union; DynamicPageEntry carries function-valued path builders with declared `requiresParams`.

nodes.name: app-settings.ts
nodes.summary: Zod schema for the runtime feature switches exposed on the Admin application-settings page: the default customer credit-warning threshold, the tier-1 finance approval VND cap (fail-closed at 0), and the salary payroll business-unit scope.

nodes.name: customer-service-finance.ts
nodes.summary: Zod contracts for customer-facing finance surfaces: customer-visible timeline events, the recoverable-costs ledger query and approval flow, debit-note send/confirm/dispute decisions, direct-money treasury payments, profitability report queries across eight dimensions, and the accounting transport register rows with readiness snapshots. Sort-key enums are documented to mirror the backend SQL whitelists.
nodes.languageNotes: Money amounts on the wire are regex-validated decimal strings (moneyStringSchema) rather than numbers, preserving financial precision across JSON boundaries; queries use `.strict()` plus cross-field `.refine()` for date ordering.

nodes.name: email-settings.ts
nodes.summary: Zod contract for the ADMIN-only Resend email credential: the API key is write-only (GET responses expose only a masked suffix), and a payload may not both replace and clear the key in the same update.

nodes.name: financial-reporting-policy.ts
nodes.summary: Zod schemas for financial reporting policy and per-truck financial profiles: Vietnam month-start effective dates, whole-VND money fields, versioned straight-line depreciation profile records, and state projections carrying current/future/history versions plus pending governance requests.
nodes.languageNotes: Money is normalized through a union of number|string transformed to canonical digit strings and compared with BigInt in superRefine; date-only strings are validated by round-tripping through UTC midnight to reject impossible calendar dates.

nodes.name: geotag.ts
nodes.summary: Shared wire contract for event-driven photo GPS geotagging: photo-bearing entity types (trip, trip-expense, company-expense photos), fix sources (phone/exif/manual), the POST /api/geotag payload with anti-replay gpsAt and warm-fix diagnostic fields, and the read-shape PhotoGeotag record. Requirements traceability comments tie accuracy/freshness gates to anti-fraud specs.

nodes.name: governance-action.ts
nodes.summary: Vocabulary and Zod contracts for the governance approval center: 25 subject types, 42 action kinds, action statuses, capabilities, allowed decisions (check/approve/reject/return/cancel), version-guarded decision payloads, and the sortable paginated list query whose sort-key enum is shared by the backend orderBy whitelist and the client.
nodes.languageNotes: Const-asserted tuple literals (`as const`) double as both the Zod enum source and the derived union types, keeping vocabulary, validation, and typing in one declaration.

nodes.name: ocr-settings.ts
nodes.summary: Zod contract for ADMIN-only OCR settings running on an OpenRouter API key, using the same write-only key semantics as the email settings: GET returns only a masked preview, omitting the key preserves it, and an explicit flag clears it.

nodes.name: shipment-charge-proposal-link.ts
nodes.summary: Zod contract for reviewing shipment charge proposals across five fee fields, discriminated by decision: ACCEPT_LINK must target a specific debit-note document and line with optimistic-concurrency versions, while REJECT requires only a mandatory reason.

nodes.name: work-inbox.ts
nodes.summary: Zod contracts for the role-based work inbox: a common item base (state, parties, blockers, next action, target route) additively extended into operations, driver, customer, accountant, manager, and admin-health projections, plus the paginated response envelope pinned to the Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh timezone and the customer delivery-response decision schema that requires a reason on dispute.
nodes.languageNotes: Role projections use `baseSchema.extend({...})` so every role-specific item retains the stable common shape — an additive schema-extension pattern that keeps consumer types decoupled.

nodes.name: shipment-effective.ts
nodes.summary: Pure effective-value resolvers for shipment container planning under the SILVER L1 program contract: factory precedence (container site authority, then shipment site, then legacy free-text factory name) and per-container fulfillment dates cast to the Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh business timezone. Every surface that needs the effective factory or planning date resolves through these helpers instead of re-deriving precedence per endpoint.
nodes.languageNotes: Local dates are computed with fixed-offset arithmetic (time + 420 minutes, then toISOString().slice(0,10)) rather than Intl or a timezone library — valid because Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh has no DST.

nodes.name: resolveEffectiveFactory
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective factory for a container through the precedence chain container-level site authority, shipment-level site, then legacy free-text factory name, returning the site id, display label slot, and which level produced the value.

nodes.name: resolveEffectiveFulfillmentDate
nodes.summary: Returns the effective fulfillment/planning date: FCL containers use their appointment cast to the Vietnam local date (allowing sibling containers to plan on different days), falling back to the shipment's expected delivery date.

nodes.name: localDateInBusinessZone
nodes.summary: Casts an ISO instant or Date to its YYYY-MM-DD local date in the +07:00 business timezone via fixed-offset arithmetic, returning null for unparseable input so callers decide between fallback and invalid.

nodes.name: listJobs
nodes.summary: Returns a snapshot array of all registered scheduler jobs.

nodes.name: lockApplicationOwnedUniqueness
nodes.summary: Takes a transaction-scoped application lock on one scope/parts uniqueness key by delegating to lockApplicationOwnedUniquenessSet.

nodes.name: persistAudit
nodes.summary: Persists an audit entry through the installed (injectable) audit persist handler.

nodes.name: currentVietnamMonthStart
nodes.summary: Computes the first day of the current month in Vietnam timezone as a YYYY-MM-01 string.

nodes.name: assertCanMakeGovernanceAction
nodes.summary: Asserts the role holds maker capability for a governance action kind, throwing 403 otherwise.

nodes.name: emitNotificationAndWait
nodes.summary: Generates and persists an in-app notification, awaiting completion so callers finish only after the durable row exists.

nodes.name: persistNotificationInTx
nodes.summary: Persists the in-app notification row inside the caller's domain transaction; push delivery stays post-commit best-effort.

nodes.name: buildGovernedConfigSnapshot
nodes.summary: Builds the governed-config snapshot envelope (resource, fingerprint, plain row) for a CRUD row.

nodes.name: governedConfigVersionFromUpdatedAt
nodes.summary: Derives a monotonic governed-config version number from the row's updatedAt timestamp.

nodes.name: proposalKey
nodes.summary: Builds the stable factId:field map key used to index shipment charge-proposal coverage.

layers.name: API Layer
layers.description: Express 5 route handlers under backend/src/routes (financial, config, trips, shipments, forwarder, portal, salary, OCR, uploads) that translate HTTP requests into service calls behind the auth/Casbin middleware chain.

layers.name: Service Layer
layers.description: Business-logic modules in backend/src/services covering shipments, trips, treasury, salary, and OPS workflows — the most cohesive layer of the graph (0.42 intra-group density) that every route group depends on.

layers.name: Data Layer
layers.description: Drizzle ORM schema modules (core, financial, ops, treasury, trips, pricing) with their exported table nodes, the shared Postgres pool client, migration utilities, drizzle.config.ts, and the deploy/*.sql staging seed tables.

layers.name: Middleware & Security
layers.description: Express middleware chain (JWT auth, Casbin RBAC guard, audit logging, error handler, material-write and forwarder guards) plus the Casbin enforcer singleton with its model.conf/policy.csv policy files.

layers.name: Backend Core
layers.description: Server bootstrap (index.ts), environment config, the shared ApiError taxonomy, cross-cutting lib utilities (redis, logger, validation, transactions, report-cache), the scheduled-job runner, and the locked-entity governance manifest.

layers.name: Data Seeding
layers.description: Idempotent seeders under backend/src/seed plus the seed.ts and seed-dashboard.ts entrypoints that populate master data, customers, ports, and AR fixtures into dev and staging databases.

layers.name: Shared Contracts & Calculations

tour.title: Bootstrap & Project Contracts
tour.description: Start at backend/src/index.ts, the process entry point with the highest fan-out in the graph (37 dependencies): it wires the middleware chain, mounts every route tree, and starts the scheduler. Alongside it, AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md are the repo's binding contracts — trunk-based workflow, mandatory QA gates, the Drizzle-only SQL policy, and the authority order when documents disagree. Read these three first and you know both how the server boots and the rules every file in this tour obeys.

tour.title: Configuration & JWT Authentication
tour.description: The first thing bootstrap touches is configuration and auth. config/index.ts validates every environment variable through a zod schema and exports one typed config object, exiting in production if required variables are missing. middleware/auth.ts then verifies Bearer tokens against a Redis blacklist and the users table, revalidating customer-link drift so admin reassignments force re-login. This layer is depended on by 78 files, so its behavior colors every request that follows.
tour.languageLesson: The zod 'parse, don't assert' pattern turns untrusted environment input into a typed object at boot — config bugs surface as startup failures with precise messages instead of runtime undefined downstream.

tour.title: Casbin RBAC Authorization
tour.description: With identity established, every route is gated by Casbin role-based access control. model.conf defines a subject/object/action request schema with wildcard matchers, while policy.csv is the actual matrix: eight roles (ADMIN, MANAGER, DISPATCHER, ACCOUNTANT, CUS, OPS, DRIVER, CUSTOMER) across ~25 resources, with inline comments documenting wave-by-wave access decisions. middleware/casbin.ts enforces the policy at route mount points and carves out route-scoped allowances for cases like dispatcher fleet CRUD.
tour.languageLesson: Casbin separates policy from code: model.conf declares matcher logic ('*' matches any object or action, effect is allow-if-any), while policy.csv holds pure data — so access changes ship as CSV edits without touching TypeScript.

tour.title: Error Taxonomy & Async Safety
tour.description: Every service in the codebase throws the same error shape. errors.ts defines the canonical ApiError class carrying an HTTP status and optional details — it has a fan-in of 158, the third-most-imported file in the graph. asyncHandler.ts wraps async route handlers so rejected promises reach the global error handler (Express 5 otherwise hangs on unhandled rejections), and errorHandler.ts maps ApiError, multer, and Postgres unique-violation errors to structured JSON responses.
tour.languageLesson: Express 5 does not catch rejected promises from handlers automatically — an async handler that throws without a next(err) wrapper leaves the request hanging until timeout. The asyncHandler higher-order function is the standard fix: it forwards any rejection to the error middleware.

tour.title: The Drizzle Data Layer
tour.description: Beneath the request machinery sits the data layer, the most depended-upon code in the project. db/schema/index.ts (fan-in 210) is a barrel re-exporting the eleven split schema modules — core, master-data, pricing, trips, costs, financial, treasury, shipments, ops — so consumers see one namespace. db/index.ts (fan-in 171) creates the pooled postgres-js Drizzle client, and lib/tx.ts provides the optional-transaction runner that lets services reuse a caller's transaction or open their own. This is the repo's Drizzle-only seam: no raw SQL lives anywhere else.
tour.languageLesson: The optional-transaction pattern (accept a tx, else open one) composes atomic operations without forcing every caller to manage transactions — a service called from inside a route's transaction joins it, and called standalone it opens its own.

tour.title: Treasury Schema: The Money Tables
tour.description: Before following request flow into services, look at what money actually looks like in the schema from Step 5. treasury_movements is an append-only book ledger where four partial unique indexes guarantee one POSTED movement per physical reference, receipt, ledger entry, and reversal — immutability enforced at the database level, not in code. payment_receipts records customer payments with received/allocated/unapplied/refunded breakdowns, idempotency hashes, and payment-contract versioning. These tables are the ground truth the ledger service in Step 10 writes to.
tour.languageLesson: Partial unique indexes (unique WHERE status = 'POSTED') encode business invariants — 'never double-post the same physical receipt' — in the database itself, so even a buggy service cannot violate them.

tour.title: Shared Contracts & Money Math
tour.description: The shared/ workspace package is the contract spine consumed by backend and frontend alike: shared/src/index.ts re-exports ~640 domain types, zod schemas, label maps, and calculation helpers. Its two most safety-critical kernels are round.ts — the round2dp banker-safe rounding function behind the project's VND financial-precision rule — and tripTotals.ts, the trip P&L engine that resolves fuel by precedence and computes totals identically on both sides of the API. When a money number must match between the React UI and the Postgres ledger, this is where it is computed.
tour.languageLesson: Floating-point money bugs are avoided by a single rounding kernel: round2dp does banker-safe 2-decimal rounding so every layer (UI preview, service, ledger posting) derives the same integer-valued VND amount from one shared function rather than three local reimplementations.

tour.title: Route Anatomy & Idempotency
tour.description: Now follow a request into the route layer. routes/financial/index.ts composes eleven sub-routers in deliberate order — payments first, so direct-money governance commands win over the generic router — and registers ~30 audit events at module load; routes/trips/index.ts does the same across nine leaves. Every write endpoint flows through idempotency.service.ts (fan-in 68): it hashes the request payload with SHA-256, replays the stored result on a repeated Idempotency-Key, and throws 409 when the same key carries a different payload. This engine, plus routes/utils/idempotency.ts extracting the header, is what makes retries safe on flaky mobile connections.
tour.languageLesson: Express matches routes in registration order, so mount order is load-bearing: putting the payments router before the generic financial router ensures POST /payments/:id/approve is not swallowed by a parameterized path like /:entity/:id.

tour.title: Maker-Checker Money Governance
tour.description: This system's defining pattern: no money mutation happens in one step. governance-policy.ts is the catalog — per-action-kind capability and role matrices plus evidence requirements — that powers authorization for every governed mutation. adjustment-governance.service.ts (fan-out 27, the widest service in the graph) requests and applies AR adjustments, trip reopen, financial close, and completed-trip cancellation across trips, ledgers, and expenses. governance-actions.routes.ts exposes the generic approval surface — check, approve, reject, return-for-evidence, cancel — that operators actually click.
tour.languageLesson: Maker-checker (separation of duties) means the requester of a financial change can never be its approver — the policy layer enforces distinct-role matrices at request time and again at apply time, so a single compromised account cannot move money alone.

tour.title: Double-Entry Ledger & Payments
tour.description: Governed mutations land in the accounting core. ledger.service.ts is the double-entry engine: entity locking, trip completion and reversal posting, vendor/carrier fee collection, and balance queries with due dates resolved from the business calendar. payments.routes.ts (fan-out 25) fronts receipts, payouts, commissions, penalties, and statements, and billing-document.service.ts persists debit notes and payment statements with overlap locking and VAT totals. profit-distribution.service.ts — the graph's most tightly coupled cluster together with the payments router — splits quarterly truck profit across cap-table owners exactly, using floor-plus-remainder-to-last arithmetic under serializable transactions.
tour.languageLesson: When splitting an integer amount across N owners, floor division loses a remainder — the 'floor + remainder-to-last' trick keeps the ledger exactly balanced: every owner gets floor(total/N) and the final owner absorbs what rounding left behind.

tour.title: Trip Lifecycle: Status Machine & Figures
tour.description: The operational heart of the trucking business. trip-shared.ts (fan-in 99) provides the Tx transaction alias every trip mutation runs under. trip-status-machine.service.ts enforces each legal status transition — role checks, guard conditions, POD evidence readiness, accounting locks, ledger posting, and AR snapshot capture — in one transaction. trip-composite.service.ts is the single write seam for the trips table after the 2026-09 split, routing each patch field to the right physical table, and trip-figure-updates.service.ts re-validates governance and locks before recosting pricing, fuel, and salary figures and cascading ledger and billing updates.
tour.languageLesson: A transactional status machine makes illegal states unrepresentable: instead of trusting callers to update status and post the ledger in the right order, one function performs guard checks, the write, the ledger posting, and the snapshot inside a single database transaction — they succeed or fail together.

tour.title: The CUS Workspace (Chứng Từ)
tour.description: The CUS (chứng từ — shipping documents) workspace is where clerks live daily, and the graph flags its read side as a tightly coupled cluster. cus-shipment-workspace-reads.service.ts builds the read model — actor scope conditions, bulk support-row loading, status buckets — while cus-workspace-builders.service.ts shapes list items, container lines with missing-field derivation, and per-actor field-access rules; the writes sibling imports this module one-way to keep reads pure. shipment-accounting-lock.service.ts is the barrel guarding the accounting-lock family so a shipment's figures freeze once they feed the ledger from Step 10.
tour.languageLesson: A one-way import boundary (writes import reads, reads never import writes) keeps a read model free of mutation side effects — the workspace can be reasoned about and cached as a pure projection of shipment state.

tour.title: Seeding & Master-Data Import
tour.description: Data enters the system two ways. seed.ts orchestrates the idempotent demo/staging seed — reference data, customers, pricing, fleet, trips, financials — hashing one shared demo password and driving every submodule. master-data-import.service.ts is the production path: Excel workbook validation, per-row classification with blocking rules, a batch analyze/apply/reject lifecycle, and idempotent apply with durable-effect cleanup. deploy/seed-vantai.sql is the raw staging seed feeding the vantai environment you will deploy in the next step.
tour.languageLesson: Idempotent seeding means running the seed twice produces the same database: every insert is an upsert keyed on natural identifiers, which is what allows staging databases to be re-synced from production seeds without duplicating rows.

tour.title: Infrastructure: Build & Deploy
tour.description: The capstone: how all of the above ships. backend/Dockerfile is a multi-stage build — a builder stage installs workspace dependencies with pnpm 10 and compiles shared plus backend TypeScript, then a minimal node:22-alpine runtime ships only pruned node_modules, dist output, Casbin policies, and Drizzle migrations. deploy/docker-compose.silversea.yml runs production on a dedicated :prod image channel with data volumes deploys never touch, while the root Makefile orchestrates the entire lifecycle from local boot through backup-first migrations to prod deployment. pnpm-workspace.yaml declares the three-package monorepo (frontend, backend, shared) that makes Steps 1-13 one build unit.
tour.languageLesson: Separate image channels (:latest for demo/staging, :prod for production) make it structurally impossible for a demo deploy to clobber the production containers — combined with multi-stage builds, the runtime image carries no compilers and no dev dependencies, shrinking both attack surface and size.
